iem-aful-performer-5.review: Such a pity. A 5BA + 1DD layout should be good, but the coherency is lacking and the crossover between drivers isn't good: it can't deliver proper detail, and there's noticeable sibilance in the upper mids/treble. Not wow, not grand. The drivers don't meet well in the mids, so it's less natural, unlike the Mangird Tea 2 or Blessing, which sound very coherent, almost like a single DD. A HALF-BAKED PRODUCT. Go straight to the Tea 2.

iem-tanchjim-nora.review: Still very Tanchjim; from the Bunny to this it's the same story: a gradual mid-bass rise from the very middle, 500 Hz, down to the sub, but small, and bright at 8 kHz. Not my cup of tea. The driver is OK, the technicalities are OK.

iem-tangzu-fu-du.review: Tangzu's first attempt at a BA + DD hybrid. Very weak, roughly like the Tanchjim Kara. The high treble from the BA pierces: shouty, unnatural. Better the Simgot EM6L, or if your budget allows, go straight to the Sound Rhyme SR5.

iem-moondrop-lan.review: An UPGRADE OF THE MOONDROP CHU, customised. More body; not very punchy, but more bass. The upper midrange is a bit nasal. Yes, the tuning leans neutral, but there's still bass, though it's not as good a neutral as the Sennheiser IE200. Still a good option. Average soundstage, but OK. I don't like the fit much, and the shells are all metal. Nice cable.

iem-trn-conch.review: An ordinary 500k single DD. Safe. Only the treble is grainy, kind of rough. I don't know how to describe it, but you'll know once you compare it with the C3 or Q1 Pro; those two are better. This one wins on accessories: a modular cable with swappable 2.5/4.4 jacks, and swappable nozzle filters that differ only slightly, like the Simgot EA500. METAL BODY: be careful of static shocks. My advice: just get the EPZ Q1 Pro or C3.

iem-tanchjim-one.review: More spacious and open, with a tidier midrange to treble and better clarity, even compared with the DFi. But get the DSP (digital signal processing) version: its USB-C plug is also a DAC that applies an EQ preset directly to the IEM (no setup needed), so it's well balanced. The bass is tidy and deep. Cool. Wider and nicer than the Tin C0, but that's a different price, mate. Detachable 2-pin, so you can still use it if you change cables one day. Best worn straight down; if you customise, my advice is skip the ear hooks. The treble can get a bit sharp at loud volume.

iem-tangzu-wan-er-2.review: Have a Wan'er SE? Keep it. Don't have one? Fine to buy. The SE has very slightly less bass and is a bit brighter. Against the white Kinera Wyvern I still prefer the Kinera (subjective: warmer, wider in the lows). The cable's ear hook isn't good; my advice is to tear it off: it's stiff and thick and pulls the fit out of the ear. Comes with Sancai eartips.

iem-cvj-vivian.review: Bass-heavy, V-shaped, but the top of the treble isn't too spicy. The driver's OK; the tonality isn't for me, against the JM-1 trend: the classic V. For basshead lovers. Suits lower volumes.

iem-gk-kunten.review: Good. Slightly less bass than the Saga, even the Balanced version, and the treble isn't higher than the Saga's either (check his squig). Very similar to the Tin C1; the C1 has a little less sub. My note: the low-mids are still a bit much for my taste, but it's OK. The nozzle looks great; hopefully there aren't many imbalance issues from sweat getting stuck in the nozzle. And the part near the ear is plastic, not metal, so hopefully no shocks in houses without grounding.

iem-kz-saga-balanced.review: KILLER BUDGET IEM OF 2025! Verrrry good tonally: well balanced, not V-shaped, cheap. It feels spacious and simply balanced. Moderate-volume lovers will surely like it. Not super punchy or boomy, just balanced. The Bass version adds a little bass and pointier treble; take this over the Bass version. It's actually not very different from the Polaris, just with more weight from mid-bass to sub-bass; I'm sure many people will like it. (Review on his YouTube.)

iem-tangzu-wan-er-studio.review: The nozzle has been improved. The tuning got even more neutral, with even less sub-bass. The tuning is fine if you want something for monitoring without much sub. But I prefer the white Kinera Wyvern, Pro or non-Pro; that one's simply better. The fit is OK and the resin is sturdy. (He notes the tuning feels thick in the sub.) (Review on his YouTube: IEMs from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

iem-cca-polaris.review: Very good value for its budget, competing with the Chu 2 and Zero 2. I find the treble pleasing too, and not too bright; a bit warm, slightly muddy. Looking at the graph, the Zero 2 at twice the price makes no sense to me, especially as the Zero's fit isn't nice. At around 100k this wins big. I also prefer its tuning to the Castor Bass. (Review on his YouTube: IEMs from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

iem-tin-hifi-elf-c0.review: Half the price of the ONE and very close in quality, in a slightly different direction: the One emphasises sub-bass more and has a slightly wider soundstage up top; the low-mids on the C0 are enjoyable, and rock and pop-punk sound fierce. The One wins on fit. But for 200k this is excellent and can beat the DFi too. Any version is OK; the DSP USB-C one is slightly warmer, otherwise the same. You can't change the cable without losing the brand's correction; for the detachable version you need a good cable + a good DAC. If you have the budget, go straight to the C2 if you want to stay with Tin HiFi. (Review on his YouTube: IEMs from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

iem-tin-hifi-c1.review: Tin HiFi drivers are never bad; their timbre is always good. Even cheap, it doesn't have the metallic iron ringing in the treble that KZ/CCA still have. Annoyingly the treble roll-off is still a bit pointy (check Fernanda's squig.link), though better than the Saga and Phoenix. But the GK Kunten can definitely rival it.

iem-cozoy-d2.review: Extremely limp, weak bass, not just in quantity: even when I boost the bass with EQ, it doesn't kick like other neutral IEMs such as the Arisyn Huo Shu and Moondrop Lan 2 Ref. So I'd say go for the Arisyn instead. Limp, plus an upper-mid-centric, bright tuning. Not recommended from me, by my subjective preference. Tough.

iem-tanchjim-bunny.review: Yet another 300k set. Upper-mid-to-treble-centric. Punchy, but not much bass: very, very little. Very Tanchjim. The driver's treble is a bit rough, an affordable driver: not harsh as in merely boosted in the lower treble/upper mids, but genuinely grainy, rough and less resolving. I prefer the white Kinera Wyvern / Tangzu Wan'er Studio. A bit better than the Chu 2 / TE Gate. For vocal lovers who want less bass. (Full review on his YouTube.)

iem-kinera-wyvern-blue.review: The safe Kinera Wyvern compared with the Qing and the purple Abyss: this one's better. It competes closely with the white one, and many people don't like the white colour; here's the answer. Pleasant. Very balanced tonality even pushed loud. Spacious vocals. Separation and imaging are very OK for under 500k. The timbre is also more natural than the white one. The mid-bass is a bit much and the upper mids still a little covered compared with the white, but it's very safe if you want a Wyvern and don't like the white colour.

iem-kz-dfi.review: DON'T BUY IT ANY MORE: LOTS OF IMBALANCE PROBLEMS. The tuning isn't V-shaped. The bass quantity isn't overdone. Clear midrange vocals; the presence boost doesn't hurt. Very lively, reverb tails clearly audible, enjoyable punch. Technically still not at the Tin HiFi C3's level, whose cymbals are natural and not harsh; KZ is still slightly rough, but very OK. A good recommendation. There's a tunable version (EQ presets on the IEM body that only raise or lower the bass); maxed out, it still has less bass than the non-tunable DFi. If you like it as neutral as the tunable, better to get the Tin C2. A pity, in my view. Can rival the BLON Z300. Swap eartips to AET08 or Type E. The mid-bass isn't muddy like the BLON; cleaner.

iem-gk-streak.review: Audiophiles love saying "so cheap and you get a planar": overglorifying planars in cheap IEMs happens a lot. The planar timbre is still lacking. Tonally it's nearly identical to the Kunten, just airier and slightly cleaner. At this budget, why not the HE Wenji, Wyvern or Tangzu? Just want the planar validation? Go ahead. (Full review on his YouTube.)

iem-truthear-gate.review: Versus the Hola, as I remember, the Hola's resolution is a bit murky (not its tuning). This is nicer: the clarity and tightness between sounds is better too. Nice if you don't like much bass; it's not too punchy. But for resolution and separation from the driver itself I prefer the Zero 2, and above all, for smoother sound, a nice fit, better value and a mic, I'd take the Kinera Wyvern, honestly. The transparent style is pretty, though; the black one especially.

iem-moondrop-chu-3.review: A bit more defined, clearer clarity than the 2, as I remember. For separation and stereo-imaging width I'd pick the Wyvern over this. The tonality is a bit muddy in the low-mids; the upper mids are safe, and the air treble isn't piercing. It's dominated by low-mids and upper mids. I've made an EQ for it (table on the right). The main weakness: the cable makes it a bit murky and less open. Swapping to a KBEAR P34 / Hazy solved this, but the cable doesn't seat fully, blocked by the shell. Verus Candy and Xinhs SCC fit.

iem-kefine-loric.review: Mild V, slightly muddy. Not my preference. (Review on his YouTube.)

iem-simgot-ew100p.review: The fit is a champion, like the Hola: a really good fit for monitoring. Balanced sound. The midrange isn't as revealing as the Wan'er and Salnotes Zero; the emphasis is definitely at the bottom of the sub-bass and the top of the presence treble, a bit like the Hola. But I think the EW100P is better. Tuning-wise I still like the Wan'er, and the Salnotes Zero if you like less bass. But this is not bad at all.

iem-tangzu-wan-er.review: Wow, the Wan'er has extraordinary quality. An enjoyable treble roll-off, clear. The mid-bass punch is OK compared with the Salnotes Zero; the sub-bass isn't as much as the QKZ HBB. Good driver resolution, not plasticky or metallic, though drivers like the Aria/C3 are still slightly better, not far behind. Build quality is very lacking: the nozzle filter comes off easily.

iem-sony-ex15c.review: Someone will always need this: a piston-shaped IEM with a straight-down cable. A VERY GOOD MIC. Volume and music controls (pause/skip/previous) right on the cable. Warm, slightly muddy sound. Suits moderate volume.

iem-cca-phoenix.review: Same old. Still grainy treble, sharp metallic treble. Upper mids down to the sub are safe; the mids are cut a bit deep around maybe 500 Hz. The timbre is still very CCA/KZ. Stay with the GK Kunten or move on to the Wyvern/Wan'er.

iem-kz-castor.review: There's a switch but it doesn't change much; just get the Bass version. Lovely for bassheads. Similar. A rather V-shaped, very KZ treble. Safe at low volume; a bit higher and it may be sharp. Want warm? Take the QKZ HBB if you're afraid of sharpness. (Review on his YouTube: IEMs from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

iem-truthear-hola.review: Just take the EW100P. The mids are a bit murky and muffled, but there's a treble boost at the top and a little more sub-bass than the Wan'er.

iem-7hz-salnotes-zero.review: Neutral with a bass boost. Not really my preference, but it's tuned really well if you're into neutral with a minimal bass boost. Technicalities aren't amazing but enough; average soundstage. I like the Tangzu Wan'er better because its bass punch is cooler; this one's a bit weak. But the upper midrange here is very clear. If you're into that, go get it.

iem-tanchjim-kara.review: Shouty treble at 8 kHz, unnatural timbre, a bad crossover from mids to highs: a sudden dip after 8 kHz so the presence goes muffled. Weird, very weird. Avoid. Buy the Simgot EM6L instead.

iem-moondrop-quarks-dsp.review: The treble roll-off is really lovely: nothing pierces or sticks out pointy at any particular frequency. The mid-bass isn't as high as the Ling Long, nor the sub-bass, so it's less bassy than the Ling Long. If you like balanced, cleaner-sounding, not muffled/bassy, take this, and get the DSP version with the USB-C plug.

iem-lafitear-lf3.review: Remember, more drivers isn't necessarily better. It's from the same factory as KZ and Nakamichi (today's cheap Nakamichi, not the high-end one of old). The Indonesian distributor is Chordozora, also a drum maker in Indonesia, so the drummers it endorses get sent these. The sound leans bright in the treble, with unnatural timbre. For the price the mids to lows are fine, but I think it's already well beaten by Tin HiFi, Moondrop, or even the Polaris. OK at low volume, spicy when loud. The fit isn't as good as the C3.

iem-phi-audio-3-14.review: Very muffled, very warm, like the Eario. I don't think it's great. The fit is excellent, but compared with today's ChiFi it's far behind the Tin C3, C2, Chu 2, Polaris, Zero 2 and Q1 Pro, whose value is very good.

iem-trn-mt1-max.review: A superb balanced budget IEM with a great tuning. The cable is really bad and makes it bright; replace it per the recommendation in the table on the right. You can change the tuning by sliding its switches with something like a safety pin; I prefer the Balanced tuning. Swap the eartips to Final Audio Type E and it's not bright any more. Lovely. Weakness at this budget: the treble still sounds veiled and the timbre a bit unnatural, but better than the MT1 Pro. No driver flex (where the driver crinkles like plastic when you insert it).

iem-qkz-x-hbb.review: Great for V-shape lovers. The driver quality is good: smooth highs that don't hurt. Very, very safe. Please stop buying cheap KZs if you like V-shape: just this. If you find it too much, take the Tangzu Wan'er.

iem-kz-ling-long.review: A nice single DD. Balanced, with very smooth treble. A laid-back soundstage. Extended sub-bass, not overdone. Smooth upper mids and treble. Nice pushed fairly loud too. Nice straight-down fit, just don't push it in too deep or the treble disappears. The only weakness is the cable can't be replaced; if it breaks one day it needs recabling (OneZero or Van Jan Cook can do it).

iem-sgor-adonis.review: Unique: 2 drivers, though the BA doesn't really sound like a BA. The mids are a bit recessed, there's lots of sub-bass compared with the Castor Bass, and the sound is a bit spicy, with an 8 kHz peak that's a bit bothersome. What I admire is the cable: thick, with a clear mic too.

iem-blon-bl01.review: A different tuning from the BL03: I like that guitar strumming comes through more, which is what the 03 lacks for me. Minus: an unusual shape for people's ears, and the midrange boost starts too early. I prefer the Tangzu Wan'er.

iem-blon-bl03.review: THE MOST LEGENDARY IEM of 2019, which broke the idea that good has to be expensive. The ChiFi (Chinese hi-fi) industry crushed the market prices of big consumer IEM brands like JBL, Bose, Sony, Sennheiser and others.

iem-kz-dq6.review: KZ is still KZ: peaky, sharp treble. Better to take the DQ6S.

iem-trn-mt1-pro.review: Just buy the MT1 Max, unless this is discounted to 50–60k.

iem-sgor-venus.review: Overhyped; I don't like it. The sound is close to the KZ EDX: still pointy and metallic at 8 kHz, with some boxiness at 300–500 Hz.

iem-cca-cra.review: V-shaped. Plastic nozzle; there are reports it melts easily.

iem-cca-cra-2.review: This can rival the KZ DQ6. Still the same, still a bit V-shaped, but fun. I think the bass rises too early, from 300 Hz, so vocals get a bit muddy. The treble is nearly identical to the KZ DQ6, still safe, a bit sharp. And of course coherent, since it isn't a triple-driver like the DQ6. Better than the NRA too, I think.
